correctness.rationale: For all m,n≥5, mixed-coordinate cliques lie in diamond or square facets, and all exceptional pure-coordinate cliques are indexed by C5 or C6 fibers. The uniform five-phase 9mn elementary collapse of the baseline diamond/square complex to its triangulated torus is justified by free-face containment, and exact finite coface checks replay all phases on representative short/long values. Each exceptional fiber attaches one (C5) or two (C6) disks along a primitive meridian or longitude after its intersection collapses to a circle. CW one-/two-cell cancellations give the stated integral homotopy types including mixed widths. Independently enumerated faces, mod-two boundary ranks and complete collapse tests corroborate boundary values but do not substitute for the all-parameter argument.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial Rips scale of Cartesian torus grids undergoes a full homotopy phase transition depending sharply on short circumference 5/6 versus long ≥7. The result uniformly classifies infinitely many previously untreated short-by-long cases, identifies the 5-by-6 mixed regime, and determines the first integral persistence kernel rather than repeating isolated square-grid Betti numbers.
